_comment: Curated supermassive black holes with direct or well-known mass measurements (stellar/gas dynamics, megamasers, reverberation mapping, EHT imaging). Coordinates are the host nuclei (J2000). 'approx: true' marks masses/distances where the literature spans a range or the method is indirect. The full AGN/quasar population (every one a supermassive black hole) loads separately and progressively from the VizieR Milliquas catalog (see js/blackholes.js).

objects.name: Sagittarius A*
objects.notes: The supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way. Mass and distance from decades of stellar-orbit monitoring; imaged directly by the Event Horizon Telescope in 2022.
objects.source: GRAVITY Collaboration 2019/2022, A&A; EHT Collaboration 2022, ApJL 930, L12

objects.name: M87*
objects.notes: Heart of the giant elliptical M87 and the first black hole ever directly imaged (EHT, April 2019). Powers a relativistic jet visible across the electromagnetic spectrum.

objects.name: Andromeda's black hole
objects.notes: The nucleus of our nearest large neighbor galaxy hosts a ~140-million-solar-mass black hole inside a distinctive double nucleus of orbiting stars.
objects.source: Bender et al. 2005, ApJ 631, 280; Kormendy & Ho 2013

objects.name: M32 nucleus
objects.notes: A compact elliptical satellite of Andromeda with a black hole of only a few million solar masses — one of the smallest galaxies known to host one.
objects.source: van den Bosch & de Zeeuw 2010; Kormendy & Ho 2013

objects.name: NGC 4258 (M106) nucleus
objects.notes: The gold standard of black-hole mass measurement: water masers trace a thin Keplerian gas disk just a fraction of a light-year from the hole.
objects.source: Herrnstein et al. 1999/2005; Miyoshi et al. 1995, Nature 373, 127

objects.name: Sombrero Galaxy black hole
objects.notes: Two-thirds of a billion solar masses in the bulge-dominated Sombrero — one of the first galaxies where a central dark mass was detected (1988).

objects.name: Centaurus A black hole
objects.notes: The nearest active radio galaxy: its black hole drives jets and giant radio lobes spanning ~10° of the southern sky.

objects.name: M81 nucleus
objects.notes: A low-luminosity active nucleus in the showpiece spiral M81, feeding at a trickle compared with quasars.

objects.name: M60 black hole
objects.notes: A 4.5-billion-solar-mass giant in the Virgo elliptical M60 — among the most massive dynamically measured holes in the local universe.

objects.name: M84 black hole
objects.notes: A Virgo radio galaxy whose nuclear gas disk, resolved by Hubble, orbits a ~billion-solar-mass hole.

objects.name: NGC 1277 black hole
objects.notes: A compact Perseus-cluster galaxy whose black hole is extraordinarily large for its host — initial estimates reached 1.7×10^10 M☉; later modeling favors ~5×10^9.
objects.source: van den Bosch et al. 2012, Nature 491, 729; Walsh et al. 2016

objects.name: NGC 4889 black hole
objects.notes: The brightest galaxy of the Coma cluster hosts one of the largest directly measured black holes: best estimate 21 billion solar masses (range 6–37).

objects.name: NGC 3842 black hole
objects.notes: Nearly ten billion solar masses in the brightest galaxy of the Leo cluster — announced alongside NGC 4889 as a record-setting pair.

objects.name: Holmberg 15A black hole
objects.notes: About 40 billion solar masses at the center of Abell 85's giant central galaxy — the largest black hole measured by direct stellar dynamics to date.

objects.name: NGC 1600 black hole
objects.notes: A 17-billion-solar-mass hole in a relatively isolated elliptical — evidence that the biggest holes are not confined to rich cluster centers.

objects.name: TON 618
objects.notes: A hyperluminous quasar whose broad-line width implies ~66 billion solar masses — among the largest estimates for any black hole. Indirect method; large uncertainty.
objects.source: Shemmer et al. 2004; Ge et al. 2019

objects.name: Cygnus A black hole
objects.notes: The archetypal powerful radio galaxy: a 2.5-billion-solar-mass engine driving jets that inflate radio lobes half a million light-years across.

objects.name: 3C 273 black hole
objects.notes: The first object recognized as a quasar (1963). Reverberation of its broad emission lines weighs the hole at just under a billion suns.

objects.name: OJ 287 primary black hole
objects.notes: A blazar whose ~12-year optical outburst cycle is modeled as a ~150-million-solar-mass secondary punching through the accretion disk of an 18-billion-solar-mass primary.

objects.name: NGC 4151 black hole
objects.notes: One of the nearest bright Seyfert 1 nuclei and a cornerstone of reverberation mapping.
objects.source: Bentz et al. 2006; Onken et al. 2014

objects.name: NGC 5548 black hole
objects.notes: The most intensively reverberation-mapped active galaxy — its black hole mass anchors the calibration used for thousands of quasars.
objects.source: Peterson et al. 2004; Pancoast et al. 2014

objects.name: NGC 3115 black hole
objects.notes: The Spindle Galaxy hosted one of the first convincing supermassive black hole detections (1992).

objects.name: NGC 4261 black hole
objects.notes: Hubble resolved a 300-light-year dusty disk feeding this radio galaxy's half-billion-solar-mass hole — an iconic early image of black hole fueling.

objects.name: M105 black hole
objects.notes: A quiet Leo-group elliptical whose ~400-million-solar-mass hole shows that even inactive galaxies keep their central engines.
objects.source: Shapiro et al. 2006; van den Bosch & de Zeeuw 2010

objects.name: NGC 7052 black hole
objects.notes: An elliptical with a 3,700-light-year dust disk orbiting its central hole, measured with Hubble spectroscopy.
objects.source: van der Marel & van den Bosch 1998, AJ 116, 2220

objects.name: NGC 1068 (M77) black hole
objects.notes: The archetype of obscured active galaxies: masers trace a warped disk around its ~10-million-solar-mass hole, hidden behind a dusty torus.

objects.name: NGC 4395 black hole
objects.notes: A dwarf spiral with no bulge at all, yet an active nucleus of only a few hundred thousand solar masses — a bridge toward intermediate-mass black holes.
objects.source: Peterson et al. 2005; den Brok et al. 2015

objects.name: NGC 6240 twin black holes
objects.notes: A galaxy merger caught with two (possibly three) supermassive nuclei only a few thousand light-years apart, destined to coalesce.
objects.source: Komossa et al. 2003, ApJL 582, L15; Kollatschny et al. 2020
